audit_name: Team A adversarial reassessment - MPI identity and clinical safety
mode: read-only static adversarial audit with synthetic reproduction designs
status_vocabulary_note: New findings carry the required lifecycle status DISCOVERED. The separate assurance_status field uses only IMPLEMENTED, TESTED, INTEGRATED, BLOCKED and NOT IMPLEMENTED. No elevated assurance status was awarded to audited work.

clinical_workflows_reviewed: Pharmacy interaction, allergy, contraindication and dose engines
verification_performed: controlled comparison with protected governance documents
known_disclosed_failure_not_reported_as_: NR-011 FK test failure under tests/identity co-collection

findings.title: Unverified lab-supplied NID short-circuits identity matching into an auto-claim
findings.owner_gate: Identity/data owner decision required for NID provenance and verification authority policy.

evidence.observation: Any nid_hash equality hit sets best_candidate, best_score=1.0 and best_method=nid_exact without checking nid_verified.
best_method == nid_exact auto-claims the citizen and records match_score 1.0 regardless of demographic disagreement.
Citizen.nid_verified is Boolean nullable=False default=False.
Genesis citizen is written with nid_verified=False.
Detached citizen is written with nid_verified=False.
Registration path writes nid_verified=False.
NID HMAC key falls back to other secrets in non-production with only a warning; key stability is a contributing control concern.

findings.reproduction: Synthetic only: seed citizen A with NID hash H and A's name/DOB/gender; seed lab patient P with B's name/DOB/gender but submit a raw national ID that hashes to H; call /mpi/resolve. Observe returned citizen A, match_method nid_exact, match_score 1.0, and nid_verified still false. No real patient data required.
findings.falsification: Finding is falsified if an authoritative verification gate blocks or downgrades an unverified nid_exact hit before auto-claim, or if a test proves nid_verified=True is required and set for this path.
findings.root_cause: The fast path treats hash equality of a submitted identifier as equivalent to verified national identity; the existing nid_verified field is not used as an authorization signal.
findings.impact: A wrong, stale or maliciously supplied NID can bind a lab patient to another person's canonical identity, propagating results and demographics to the wrong record. This is distinct from AUD-01 review-reject and AUD-04 concurrency race.
findings.severity_rationale: Wrong-patient identity linkage is a high-harm safety failure; exposure is not universal because an incorrect NID input or stale upstream identifier is required.
findings.remediation: Require an authoritative verification signal before nid_exact score 1.0; otherwise downgrade to probabilistic scoring and force pending_review when demographics disagree; persist verification provenance and reviewer; add a synthetic regression test asserting an unverified NID cannot auto-claim.
alternatives: NID verification service assertion with cache expiry.
Dual-factor match requiring NID plus DOB and name agreement.
findings.verification_scope: Static source and grep analysis plus synthetic reproduction design; no runtime execution.

findings.title: Latent non-atomic canonical auto-create has no lock or DB uniqueness fence
findings.owner_gate: Full fence depends on MP-001 / ODR-004 schema and canonical-hardening decisions.

evidence.observation: find_or_create_canonical performs get-then-insert for CanonicalPatient and link rows without acquiring a canonical link lock.
acquire_canonical_link_lock is imported.
Lock is used in an explicit link function, not in find_or_create_canonical.
Lock is used in the second explicit link function, not in find_or_create_canonical.
PatientLink and CitizenLink have indexes but no unique constraints on patient_id or citizen_id.

findings.reproduction: Synthetic design only: if a future caller invokes find_or_create_canonical for the same patient from two sessions, both can observe no existing canonical, insert two canonical rows and two links, and a later first() lookup can strand one canonical. Static grep found no current caller.
findings.falsification: Finding is falsified if all callers are proven to hold the same advisory lock with DB uniqueness, or if the helper is removed or converted to the locked link service.
findings.root_cause: The helper uses a check-then-insert pattern while the repository's canonical write discipline was added only to explicit link endpoints.
findings.impact: Dormant split-identity risk if the helper is wired into national onboarding; overlaps MP-001 but is a distinct code path.
findings.severity_rationale: Low because there are currently no callers; likelihood rises immediately if national onboarding adopts the helper.
findings.remediation: Acquire the canonical link lock inside the helper, re-check under lock, use conflict-safe insert, and require MP-001 uniqueness before exposing callers; add a concurrency test before first use.
alternatives: Convert it to a thin wrapper over the locked link service.
findings.verification_scope: Static source and grep analysis; no runtime execution.

findings.title: Critical-result notification workflow returns false success without emitting any notification, event, audit or outbox record
findings.owner_gate: Clinical owner must define recipient, escalation and acknowledgement policy; outbox implementation itself is engineering work.

evidence.observation: Module docstring states every workflow emits events for notification, audit and external systems via the outbox pattern.

process_critical_result queries the result, computes notification_window and returns status alerted with action notify_ordering_physician; no notification, event, outbox, audit or delivery record is created.
CriticalResultDetected event class exists but grep found no emitter or call site.
The endpoint returns the no-op process_critical_result value directly to the caller.

findings.reproduction: Synthetic only: create a synthetic Result with is_critical=true and is_panic=true in a synthetic lab; call the critical-result endpoint or process_critical_result; observe response status alerted and action notify_ordering_physician while notification/outbox/audit/event tables and the event bus remain unchanged. No real patient data required.
findings.falsification: Finding is falsified if a test demonstrates that the workflow emits a durable CriticalResultDetected event or outbox/notification/audit record with delivery tracking and acknowledgement semantics on the same call.
findings.root_cause: The workflow implements only metadata computation; the documented steps 2-4 (log alert, determine pathway, trigger outbound notification) have no integration with the notification or outbox layer.
findings.impact: A critical or panic result can appear handled in API responses while no clinician is notified, creating delayed treatment, patient harm and medico-legal false assurance.
findings.severity_rationale: Missed critical-result notification can cause immediate harm or death; detectability is low because the API returns a success state.
findings.remediation: Implement transactional outbox/event emission with durable delivery attempts and acknowledgement state; fail the endpoint if no notification can be enqueued; write an audit row with actor, result, recipient and time; add tests that assert zero-alert and delivered-alert states distinctly.
alternatives: Synchronous notification adapter with explicit failure propagation.
External LIMS alert bridge with a durable reconciliation check.
Capability-gated manual escalation queue until automated delivery is verified.
findings.verification_scope: Static source, event-definition and call-site analysis plus synthetic reproduction design; no runtime execution.

findings.title: Auto-validation omits patient gender and age, permitting wrong reference interval and critical detection
findings.owner_gate: Clinical/data owner must define authoritative demographic-specific reference ranges and fail-closed behavior for missing ranges.

evidence.observation: auto_validate_result exposes patient_age_days and patient_gender as optional arguments.
Gender and age filters are applied only when arguments are provided; selection orders by lab_id and gender descending with nulls last.
The manual auto-validate endpoint passes only result value, test code, lab_id and instrument_id.
Result creation passes only value, test code, lab_id and instrument_id.

findings.reproduction: Synthetic only: configure two active ranges for the same test, one pediatric/female and one adult/generic with different critical_high; create a synthetic pediatric female result whose value is critical under the pediatric range but normal under the adult range; invoke either auto-validation call site. Observe that no gender/age filters are applied and a generic or wrong-specificity range can be selected. Falsification requires the call sites to pass demographics and a test proving the correct range is selected.
findings.falsification: Finding is falsified if all auto-validation call sites pass patient_age_days and patient_gender and regression tests prove the demographic-specific range is selected, with fail-closed behavior when no matching range exists.
findings.root_cause: Patient context is available in the caller layers but is dropped at the API boundary; the engine treats demographics as optional and silently falls back to generic ranges.
findings.impact: Abnormal or critical results can be reported as normal and auto-validated, or receive the wrong flag, especially for neonates, children and sex-specific analytes.
findings.severity_rationale: Both reachable call sites omit demographics, making exposure high; partial flags may provide some detection, so detectability is medium.
findings.remediation: Derive age in days and gender from the patient record at every call site and pass them explicitly; enforce required demographics for range-governed tests; log the selected range id and applied filters; add synthetic tests for pediatric, adult, male, female and missing-range cases.
alternatives: Resolve ranges in a dedicated clinical-range service that fetches demographics by result id.
Fail validation and route to manual review whenever demographic-specific ranges cannot be resolved.
findings.verification_scope: Static source and call-site analysis plus synthetic reproduction design; no runtime execution.

findings.title: Auto-validation critical flags are not persisted by the route, so critical-result workflow skips the result

evidence.observation: Critical high/low conditions append flags and warnings only to the returned dictionary.
The route commits only validation_status, auto_validated and auto_validated_at when auto_validated is true; it does not persist flags, is_critical, is_abnormal or flag.
process_critical_result returns skipped when Result.is_critical is false.
The result-creation service persists critical/abnormal flags, showing an inconsistent second write path.

findings.reproduction: Synthetic only: create a synthetic result whose value exceeds configured critical_high; call the manual auto-validate endpoint; observe the response contains critical_high and a warning while Result.is_critical remains false and no commit of flags occurs; then call the critical-result endpoint and observe status skipped. Falsification requires post-commit assertion that every critical_* response flag persists is_critical=true.
findings.falsification: Finding is falsified if a single validation-application path persists all flags and status fields before commit and a test proves the critical-result endpoint subsequently reports alerted for the same result.
findings.root_cause: The route consumes only the auto_validated subset of the validation result; flag application exists in a different service path, leaving two divergent handoffs.
findings.impact: A result detected as critical by validation can be invisible to the critical-result notification workflow, compounding AUD-CLIN-001 and allowing release/escalation decisions based on incomplete state.
findings.severity_rationale: Loss of the critical flag at a handoff can suppress escalation; exposure requires the manual route path, so likelihood is medium.
findings.remediation: Centralize application of validation outcomes in one function used by both route and service paths; persist is_critical, is_abnormal, flag, validation_status and audit data in the same transaction; add endpoint-pair regression tests.
alternatives: Make the critical-result workflow derive criticality from validation flags instead of Result.is_critical.
Reject the auto-validate response unless a post-commit persistence assertion passes.
findings.verification_scope: Static source and divergent-path analysis plus synthetic reproduction design; no runtime execution.

findings.title: Pharmacy clinical engines ignore lab_id and select arbitrary or cross-tenant rules
findings.owner_gate: Clinical formulary/data owner must define rule source, version and tenant-scope policy.

evidence.observation: DrugInteractionEngine stores lab_id but its query has no lab/tenant predicate and returns q.first().
ContraindicationEngine stores lab_id but queries drug and condition only, returning all matches without lab scope.
AllergyEngine stores lab_id but returns q.first() from an unscoped drug/allergen query.
DoseEngine stores lab_id but DoseGuideline query filters only drug/indication/age/weight and returns all results.
Renal adjustment uses an unscoped first() rule.
TenantMixin only declares a lab_id column; it does not install automatic query scoping.
Routes construct the engines with user.lab_id, which the engines never apply.

findings.reproduction: Synthetic only: seed two synthetic labs with conflicting rules for the same drug pair, allergy or dose guideline; instantiate the engine with lab B's id; observe that returned rules can originate from lab A or from arbitrary first/all ordering. Falsification requires a test asserting every returned rule lab_id equals the caller's lab_id and that ambiguous rule sets are rejected.
findings.falsification: Finding is falsified if every engine query applies the caller's lab/tenant scope with deterministic ordering and a cross-tenant synthetic test proves no foreign rule is returned.
findings.root_cause: Engines accept and store lab_id as a parameter but never incorporate it into query predicates; underlying mixins provide a column only, not automatic tenant isolation.
findings.impact: Missed interactions, wrong allergy warnings, wrong dose guidance or cross-tenant rule leakage can influence medication decisions.
findings.severity_rationale: Clinical rule leakage or arbitrary selection can cause medication harm; exposure depends on multiple labs and conflicting rules, so likelihood is medium.
findings.remediation: Apply tenant/lab predicates to every clinical rule query; add deterministic ordering and rule source/version pinning; reject ambiguous sets instead of using first(); log rule id/version; add cross-tenant regression tests for all four engines.
alternatives: Repository-level tenant-scoped query base that makes unscoped rule reads impossible.
Owner-approved centrally governed rule set with explicit cross-lab publication and versioning.
findings.verification_scope: Static source, mixin and call-site analysis plus synthetic reproduction design; no runtime execution.
